Fourth down: go, kick or punt?

Pick a game situation. Two methods answer: the standard one-step analysis, with how many of the bootstrap refits agree, and the exact solution of the whole game for two identical teams. Every number comes from a precomputed grid; nothing is fitted or interpolated in your browser.

This page was built from a synthetic test bundle: the numbers are made up.

Loading data...

Every fourth down in this situation. Full colour: 83% or more of the refits agree with the call; paler: 67% to 83%; grey: too close to call. Tap a cell to select it.

Models. One step: a gradient-boosted win-probability model and play-outcome models fitted on the 2010 to 2023 seasons; confidence from refits on resampled whole games (the rule of Brill, Yurko and Wyner, arXiv 2311.03490: confident at 83% agreement, lean at 67%). Exact: the game solved by backward induction on a 5-second clock grid.

Limits. The exact game has identical, league-average teams that both play optimally afterwards, and ignores the spread. Conversion chances where coaches almost never go for it are extrapolated from third downs. Bootstrap intervals are somewhat too narrow. No overtime (a tie is worth one half). The exact game treats 11 to 15 yards to go as one bin.

Grid. The team with the ball holds 3 timeouts and does not receive the second-half kickoff. Per-action intervals are left out of this page to keep it small; the Streamlit app in the same repository shows them.
